hints: Write the general $n$-th term formula for the arithmetic progression: $u_n = a + (n-1)d = 5 + 6(n-1) = 6n - 1$.
Find the first term strictly greater than 150 by solving $6n - 1 > 150$, giving the first integer index $n_1 = 26$ ($u_{26} = 155$).
Find the last term strictly less than 400 by solving $6n - 1 < 400$, giving the last integer index $n_2 = 66$ ($u_{66} = 395$).
Calculate the number of terms $N = 66 - 26 + 1 = 41$, and use the sum formula $S = \frac{N}{2}(\text{first} + \text{last})$.
walkthrough:
Express the general $n$-th term formula for the AP with $a = 5$ and $d = 6$:
$$u_n = a + (n - 1)d = 5 + 6(n - 1) = 6n - 1$$

Find the first term strictly greater than $150$ ($u_n > 150$):
$$6n - 1 > 150 \implies 6n > 151 \implies n > 25.17 \implies n_1 = 26 \quad (u_{26} = 6(26) - 1 = 155)$$

Find the last term strictly less than $400$ ($u_n < 400$):
$$6n - 1 < 400 \implies 6n < 401 \implies n < 66.83 \implies n_2 = 66 \quad (u_{66} = 6(66) - 1 = 395)$$

Calculate the number of terms $N$ and compute their sum:
$$N = 66 - 26 + 1 = 41\text{ terms}$$
$$S = \frac{N}{2}(u_{26} + u_{66}) = \frac{41}{2}(155 + 395) = \frac{41}{2}(550) = 41 \times 275 = 11275$$
